headline: Sequential margin recovery, GAAP results lean on one-off
summary_short: Net sales fell 6.8% y/y to $3,517M and ongoing (non-GAAP) EBIT dropped 69.1% to $62M, but GAAP net earnings rose 35.4% y/y to $88M, lifted by a $139M gain on the Beko stake sale that offset $41M of restructuring costs.
summary_long: Revenue fell 6.8% y/y on North America volume softness and unfavorable Latin America/SDA price-mix, offset partly by new pricing actions driving 8% sequential net sales growth and 240bps sequential EBIT margin gain in North America. Ongoing (non-GAAP) EBIT margin compressed to 1.8% from 5.3% on tariffs, raw material/fuel inflation and volume decline. GAAP operating profit fell less (-20% y/y) than ongoing EBIT (-69%) since a $139M Beko stake-sale gain offset $41M restructuring costs. Whirlpool completed a $2B ABL facility and issued $2B secured bonds, clearing debt maturities until 2028; cash rose to $1,239M, long-term debt to $6,840M. FY2026 revenue (~$15.0B)/margin outlook unchanged; EPS guidance updated to $2.25-$2.75 GAAP / $2.50-$3.00 ongoing on higher interest expense; FCF guidance $300M+.
confidence_notes: Regeneration: this summary was force-regenerated per explicit instruction; no prior WHR_US_FY2026_Q2 summary existed on disk before this run, so this is a fresh compose, not an overwrite of prior analysis. Reconciliation quirk: the resolver's SEC-XBRL 'net_income_usd_m' ($88M, tag NetIncomeLoss) is total company net earnings before deducting $13M of mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends; the press release's own headline figure is 'net earnings available to Whirlpool common shareholders' of $75M ($88M − $13M preferred dividends, since noncontrolling interest was $0 this quarter). Diluted EPS of $1.15 is computed off the $75M common-shareholder figure, not the $88M ledger total, which is why $88M / 65.2M diluted shares ($1.35) does not equal the reported $1.15 EPS. 'Ongoing EPS diluted' delta marked 'nm' per the release's own notation (swung from +$1.34 to -$0.21, a sign flip that makes a percentage change not meaningful). Free cash flow figures in the release are six-months-ended-June-30 (H1 2026: -$1,108M vs H1 2025: -$856M), not quarter-only; omitted from the KPI table to avoid mixing periods, referenced only in confidence notes. EPS guidance range is described by the release as 'updated ... reflecting new interest expense outlook' but the release does not restate the specific prior range for direct before/after comparison, so guidance.move is left null for the EPS lines rather than inferring a direction (see guidance array). Revenue and margin guidance are explicitly stated as 'unchanged' in the release's own bullet language, supporting guidance.move='held' for those two lines.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites sequential margin expansion from pricing execution, cost take-out progress and product innovation; CFO cites completion of a $2B ABL facility and $2B secured bond issuance extending debt maturities to 2028.
North America volume declined on industry contraction; Latin America and SDA Global saw negative price/mix and lower retailer inventory, partially offset by favorable pricing actions.
North America EBIT margin was pressured by volume decline plus tariff, raw material and fuel cost inflation; Latin America hit by unfavorable price/mix in Brazil, partly offset by a tax-case gain.
Fell 69% y/y as the same tariff/input-cost and volume pressures hit all three segments; North America partially offset by pricing, but not enough to hold ongoing margin.
Declined less than ongoing EBIT because GAAP included a $139M gain on the Beko stake sale, which more than offset $41M of restructuring costs excluded from the ongoing measure.
Rose y/y despite lower operating profit, helped by a GAAP tax rate of 3.5% (vs 23.9% a year ago) and a smaller equity-method investment loss.

Fell slightly y/y even though net earnings available to Whirlpool common shareholders rose, because diluted share count grew to 65.2M from 56.1M and $13M of new preferred dividends reduced earnings available to common holders.
Built up from completing a $2B asset-based lending facility and issuing $2B in secured bonds, per the CFO, extending debt maturities to 2028.
Increased on $524M of common stock issuance and $557M of mandatory convertible preferred stock issuance during H1 2026, per the financing-activities section of the cash flow statement.
